questions.question: Which statement best describes narrow AI?

options.A: AI built for a specific task such as image classification
options.B: AI that matches full human intelligence

questions.explanation: Narrow AI performs specific tasks; general AI matching humans does not yet exist.

questions.question: What is machine learning in simple terms?

options.A: Algorithms improving through data exposure

questions.explanation: ML learns patterns from data rather than relying on hand-coded rules.

questions.question: Which is an example of generative AI?

options.A: A model writing a new paragraph on request

questions.explanation: Generative AI creates new content such as text or images.

questions.question: Which AI area handles human language understanding?

options.A: Natural language processing

questions.explanation: NLP focuses on understanding and generating human language.

questions.question: Which is a likely source of bias in AI?

options.A: Training data underrepresenting some groups

questions.explanation: Unrepresentative training data is a common source of bias.

questions.question: Which quality is critical for AI in healthcare or finance?

options.A: Explainability so humans can review decisions

questions.explanation: High-stakes AI needs explainability for trust and validation.

questions.question: What is data drift?

options.A: Input distribution changing over time vs training data

questions.explanation: Drift degrades accuracy when production data differs from training data.

questions.question: Why monitor AI after deployment?

options.A: Performance can degrade as data and usage change

questions.explanation: Drift and changing behavior require ongoing monitoring.

questions.question: What does robustness mean for AI?

options.A: Coping with noisy or adversarial inputs safely

questions.explanation: Robust systems handle edge cases without dangerous failures.

questions.question: Which practice improves fairness?

options.A: Reviewing data and results for group disparities

questions.explanation: Check outcomes across groups and fix root causes.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a training set?

options.A: Provide examples for the model to learn from

questions.explanation: Training data teaches the model patterns to apply later.

questions.question: What is a validation set used for?

options.A: Tune choices without touching the final test set

questions.explanation: Validation supports tuning and detects overfitting early.

questions.question: Which metric matters most when missing positives is costly?

options.A: Recall

questions.explanation: Recall measures actual positives successfully found.

questions.question: What does overfitting mean?

options.A: Learning training data too closely and failing on new data

questions.explanation: Overfit models capture noise that does not generalize.

questions.question: What is a confusion matrix used for?

options.A: Summarize correct and incorrect predictions by class

questions.explanation: It shows true/false positives and negatives by class.

questions.question: Which task is regression?

options.A: Predicting a numeric house price

questions.explanation: Regression predicts continuous numeric outcomes.

questions.question: What is feature engineering?

options.A: Creating or transforming inputs so models learn better

questions.explanation: Good features help models learn more effectively.

questions.question: What is cross-validation for?

options.A: Estimate generalization across data splits

questions.explanation: Multiple splits give a reliable performance estimate.

questions.question: Why is defining expected results hard for AI?

options.A: Outputs can be probabilistic or lack a single right answer

questions.explanation: Use tolerances, statistics, or reference comparisons.

questions.question: What is an oracle problem in AI testing?

options.A: Difficulty knowing the correct expected output

questions.explanation: Without known answers, use metamorphic or statistical checks.

questions.question: Why run AI tests multiple times?

options.A: Results may vary across runs

questions.explanation: Nondeterminism means one run may mislead.

questions.question: What is metamorphic testing useful for?

options.A: Checking expected input-output relations when exact answers are unknown

questions.explanation: Example: rotating an image should not change its label.

questions.question: Why test AI explanations?

options.A: Users must trust and verify important decisions

questions.explanation: Clear reasons support trust and debugging.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: Why verify label quality?

options.A: Wrong labels teach wrong behavior

questions.explanation: Bad labels directly corrupt supervised learning.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: Why check for missing values?

options.A: Missing data can bias or break training

questions.explanation: Handle or document gaps before training.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: Why check class balance?

options.A: Severe imbalance can make the model ignore rare classes

questions.explanation: Imbalanced data may need sampling or weighting.

questions.question: Why test on unseen data?

options.A: Measure true generalization

questions.explanation: Held-out data reveals overfitting.

questions.question: What is a baseline model for?

options.A: Compare whether a complex model adds value

questions.explanation: Beat a simple baseline before trusting complexity.

questions.question: Why test data pipelines before training?

options.A: Broken pipelines silently corrupt models

questions.explanation: Validate data flow early to avoid wasted training.

questions.question: What should a smoke test of an ML model check?

options.A: Basic predictions work end to end

questions.explanation: Smoke tests catch wiring errors quickly.

questions.question: What is precision in classification?

options.A: Share of predicted positives that are truly positive

questions.explanation: Precision focuses on correctness of positive predictions.

questions.question: What is recall in classification?

options.A: Share of actual positives the model finds

questions.explanation: Recall focuses on coverage of real positives.

questions.question: What is deep learning?

options.A: ML using multi-layer neural networks

questions.explanation: Deep networks learn hierarchical features from data.

questions.question: Why test AI for safety?

options.A: Wrong outputs can cause real harm

questions.explanation: Safety testing limits harmful failures.

questions.question: What is A/B testing for models?

options.A: Compare two versions on live traffic subsets

questions.explanation: Live comparison reveals real-world winners.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: Why check data ranges?

options.A: Out-of-range values signal bugs

questions.explanation: Range checks catch sensor or entry errors.

questions.question: Why test model latency?

options.A: Slow models can miss product requirements

questions.explanation: Response time is part of quality.

questions.question: Why version models and data?

options.A: Reproduce results and roll back safely

questions.explanation: Versioning links each model to its exact data.

questions.question: What is transparency in AI?

options.A: Openly sharing how the system works and its limits

questions.explanation: Transparency builds justified trust.

questions.question: What is an AI agent in simple terms?

options.A: Software that perceives and acts to meet goals

questions.explanation: Agents sense environments and take actions toward objectives.
